correctness.rationale: An explicit invertible breadth-first forest encoding converts all intermediate image ranks to counts of vertices with descendants at a fixed depth, up to at most s fixed roots. The exact root-degree coefficient proves s is tight. The standard empirical-fringe law for conditioned critical geometric Galton–Watson trees gives survival probability 1/(k+1) by a checked recursion; boundedness gives L2. The embedded checker exhausted n=1..10 (23,713 maps), independently comparing literal image sets against descendant counting. No finite test is used as an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: An m-potency index does not determine intermediate image ranks (constant [4] and (1,1,3,3) are both idempotent but have ranks 1 and 2). The counted fixed-point spectra likewise do not directly supply ranks of nonstabilized powers. The generic fringe theorem covers the limiting tree statistic after the forest encoding, which is openly acknowledged as prior probabilistic machinery.

value.rationale: Iterated image rank is a canonical transformation-semigroup invariant that is not determined by final stabilization time. The infinite harmonic decay law supplies a structural scale for every fixed power in uniformly random Catalan maps. The bridge to Galton–Watson fringe survival is mathematically motivated and supports future quantitative and growing-power questions. This is neither a small isolated enumeration nor a renamed fixed-point count.
